answer: Work is witnessed at dawn and cannot be backdated, so every claim needs a live witness. An identity needs two holders outside its own cluster to countersign its claim, and one countersignature backs one identity, so n aliases need n distinct witnesses rather than one crew. Each claim is priced by rank: the k-th filing costs k squared in bond, so a farm pays near n cubed while still needing unrelated guarantors. A sable audit replays a random claim each epoch; each record carries a walnut token that cannot be transferred, and an unconfirmed claim forfeits its bond.
